title: Understanding Correlation
text: The correlation between two variables indicates how one variable changes with respect to the other. A correlation of $$1$$ or $$-1$$ means perfect linear relationship, while $$0$$ means no linear relationship.

title: Correlation and Scalar Multiples
text: If one variable is a scalar multiple of another, their correlation would be exactly $$1$$ or $$-1$$. Check the correlation between $$critic_1$$ and $$critic_2$$ to see if this is the case.

title: Evaluating the Correlation
text: What is the correlation between $$critic_1$$ and $$critic_2$$?

title: Non-Unique Solutions
text: A non-unique solution in a linear model can occur if there is perfect multicollinearity, meaning one predictor is a perfect linear combination of others. Consider the correlation values to determine if this is the case.

title: Checking for Scalar Multiples
text: Based on the correlation, is $$critic_1$$ a scalar multiple of $$critic_2$$?
